turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Krishnan, good afternoon. Sit here, please. Blood pressure is 138 over 86, pulse 76.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, sister. I am sorry we are a little late; the parking was quite difficult today.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): That is all right. Before the doctor calls you, your wife said you snore very loudly at night and you are tired through the day.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): With respect, sister, that is not correct. I do not snore, and I am not tired in the daytime. I sleep quite well.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr Krishnan. Headache, is it?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. I have been having headaches since many years, but for the past two weeks... well, actually, it is three weeks now. The pattern itself has changed.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): How?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): They are worse in the morning time, a pressure sort of pain. And I have vomited on two mornings.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): The old headaches were migraine?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Those were on one side, and light used to bother me. These feel different.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, doctor.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any blurring of vision? Any weakness in the hands or legs?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. Vision is clear, and there is no weakness. Yesterday morning I felt a little giddy, only for a few minutes, then it passed.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicines?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I take Suminat 50 milligrams when a bad headache starts, almost four times in a week nowadays. For a milder one I take Crocin, two tablets.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still on the preventive? Inderal?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I stopped the Inderal in March. It was 40 milligrams once a day, but I was feeling very dull, so I left it.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the naproxen from the old note?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I never took that, doctor. I did not even buy it.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergy?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): None, doctor.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Smoking? Drink?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I take a small whisky on the weekends only.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): All right. Follow my finger. Pupils are equal and reacting. No neck stiffness.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Squeeze my fingers. Power is normal in both arms and both legs. Plantars are down-going.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): That is a relief. My wife remains anxious about the snoring, but I do feel she is overstating it. I have a review meeting at the office after this, so I hope we can finish in good time.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Examination is normal. This may be a change in your migraine. I cannot rule out a pressure problem inside the head.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I see. Kindly advise me what is to be done.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the morning headaches and vomiting have not settled in two weeks, I will arrange a CT scan of the head.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): May I continue the same tablets until then?
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Keep Suminat 50 for the severe attacks, not more than two days in a week. Crocin for the mild ones, maximum four tablets in a day.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): And the Inderal, should I restart it?
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Leave it stopped. Come back in two weeks. If you vomit more, or the headache becomes sudden and severe, come back sooner.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I will follow that carefully.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): I will book your review for two weeks at reception, Mr Krishnan.
